newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq says U.S. holding up humanitarian purchases.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says U.S. holding up humanitarian purchases.

text.p: Iraq's foreign minister has complained to the United Nations that the United States is delaying and blocking contracts for the purchase of humanitarian goods under an "oil-for-food" deal.

Foreign Minister Mohammed al-Sahaf, in a letter circulated on Wednesday, asked Secretary-General Kofi Annan to "take positive steps to prevail upon the United States of America to desist from hindering the processing of contracts for foodstuffs and medical supplies and from using this matter as a political tool."

Under the "oil-for-food" deal that took effect last December, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy humanitarian goods, as an exception to the sanctions imposed on Baghdad after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Sahaf said that, between April 21 and 23, the United States placed a hold on 40 contracts for urgently-needed medical supplies that required the approval of the Security Council's Iraqi sanctions committee. Contracts need the consent of all 15 committee members.
He also said the United States had rejected a contract for the purchase of rice from Vietnam and six for the purchase from Jordan of sugar, cooking oil, cleaning materials and soap.
Up to April 22, he added, the sanctions committee had approved only 118 contracts out of a total of 482 submitted.
Sahaf also complained that none of the proposals he made last month, during a visit to New York, for improving the procedures of the committee had yet been acted on.
